The backbone is then trained with both classification and text-alignment objectives to learn discriminative and semantically structured motion representations while accounting for the class imbalance present in the training data. We subsequently adapt the learned backbone independently to each source domain so that the model can capture domain-specific motion characteristics. The resulting source-specific models are then merged at the parameter level to consolidate complementary knowledge across source domains into a single domain-generalized model. To further mitigate class imbalance, we perform GPT-5.5-based pseudo labeling, and our final merged models for each site do not use any class-prior correction during inference. The resulting model is evaluated under the unseen-site setting of the MoCha Challenge, using Macro F1 as the primary evaluation metric. Our method achieves a macro-F1 of 0.57 on the hidden test set with only 637K active parameters at inference, ranking 3rd among 58 leaderboard entries in the MoCha 2026 Challenge. The challenge attracted 1,669 submissions from 112 participants and offered monetary prizes sponsored by Machine Medicine Technologies.

AI.tldr: A language-aligned, domain-generalizable gait severity estimator using a Bi-GRU SMPL representation, with offline captioning via Qwen, domain-specific adaptation and parameter-level merging, plus GPT-5.5 pseudo-labeling; achieves macro-F1 0.57 on unseen MoCha data with 637k parameters, ranking 3rd.
AI.motivation: Goal: achieve domain-generalization for UPDRS-Gait severity estimation across heterogeneous clinical domains by learning semantically structured motion representations aligned with language, addressing class imbalance and leveraging language guidance.
AI.method: Bi-GRU backbone models temporal SMPL dynamics; offline motion captions generated with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; train with classification and text-alignment objectives; adapt the backbone independently to each source domain; merge source-domain models at the parameter level; apply GPT-5.5-based pseudo labeling to mitigate class imbalance; final merged models at each site avoid class-prior correction during inference; evaluate under unseen-site MoCha Challenge using Macro F1.
AI.result: Macro-F1 of 0.57 on the hidden test set; 637K active parameters at inference; ranked 3rd among 58 leaderboard entries in MoCha 2026 Challenge; MoCha challenge attracted 1,669 submissions from 112 participants.
AI.conclusion: Language-aligned motion representations combined with domain-specific adaptation and parameter-level merging enable competitive domain-generalized UPDRS-Gait estimation with a compact model, validated on an unseen-site benchmark (MoCha 2026).

title: Beyond Contact Sensors: Deep learning with Pseudo-Labeling for remote Photoplethysmography
summary: Heart rate is a critical biomarker of health, and remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) enables its contactless estimation from video data for telemedicine applications. Recent advancements in deep learning based rPPG methods achieve state-of-the-art results, outperforming classical signal-processing methods in complex scenarios. However, deep learning methods depend on datasets with precise synchronization between videos and ground truth signals collected via contact sensors, whereas signal-processing-based methods do not. To address this dependence on labeled datasets, which are labor-intensive to collect, we investigate under which circumstances pseudo-labels extracted using unsupervised signal-processing methods can replace contact sensors labels for training deep learning methods. Our systematic evaluations found that for datasets with imperfect synchronization, the pseudo-label approach outperforms supervised training on contact sensors. For datasets with good synchronization, results are mixed: within-dataset evaluation shows no significant difference between training methods, while cross-dataset evaluation favors supervised training. However, removing a single outlier participant significantly improves the pseudo-label approach's cross-dataset performance, highlighting the importance of label quality. These results demonstrate that signal-processing methods can generate valid training signals for deep learning models, reducing dependency on labor-intensive dataset collection while maintaining competitive performance.

AI.tldr: Pseudo-labels from unsupervised signal-processing methods can train deep-learning rPPG models effectively, especially when video-ground-truth synchronization is imperfect; with good synchronization, results vary; cross-dataset performance improves notably after removing an outlier; overall, reduces labeling needs while maintaining competitive performance.
AI.motivation: Reduce reliance on labor-intensive, precisely synchronized ground-truth labels for training deep-learning rPPG models by using pseudo-labels from unsupervised signal-processing methods.
AI.method: Systematic experiments comparing deep-learning rPPG models trained with pseudo-labels derived from unsupervised signal-processing against models trained with ground-truth contact-sensor labels. Evaluations include within-dataset and cross-dataset performance across datasets with varying synchronization quality, and analysis of outlier impact on cross-dataset results.
AI.result: Pseudo-label training outperforms supervised training on datasets with imperfect synchronization. On well-synchronized datasets, within-dataset performance shows no significant difference, while cross-dataset results favor supervised training unless an outlier is removed. The presence of a single outlier participant significantly affects cross-dataset performance of pseudo-labels, underscoring the importance of label quality.
AI.conclusion: Signal-processing-derived pseudo-labels can be viable training signals for deep-learning rPPG models, enabling reduced reliance on labelling with contact sensors while maintaining competitive performance; dataset synchronization quality and outlier handling are key factors shaping effectiveness.

title: UOT-Gap: A Variational Principle for the Modality Gap in Vision-Language Models via Unbalanced Optimal Transport
summary: Vision-language models such as CLIP embed images and text in a shared space, where modality-specific distributions often remain separated. Existing accounts connect this modality gap to initialization, contrastive dynamics, and information imbalance, while its distributional and pairwise contributions to retrieval remain unresolved. We introduce UOT-Gap, a training-free variational diagnostic that models frozen image and text embeddings with unbalanced entropic optimal transport (UOT). The UOT optimum separates transport, coupling complexity, and marginal mass variation; a complementary pair-aware residual compares observed image-caption pairs with the UOT soft matching. On Flickr8K and COCO-1K with frozen CLIP, OpenCLIP, and SigLIP encoders, caption degradation reduces Flickr8K Recall@1 from 0.559 to 0.003. Across six dataset-model conditions, the pair-aware residual tracks retrieval degradation with mean absolute Spearman 0.973, compared with 0.392 for the mean gap. The association remains stable across five random COCO-1K subsets at $0.954\pm0.026$, with a minimum of 0.943. UOT barycentric updates reduce the transport objective while degrading retrieval, distinguishing geometric objective descent from task improvement. These results establish UOT-Gap as a diagnostic for caption quality, modality alignment, and retrieval robustness.

AI.tldr: A training-free variational diagnostic (UOT-Gap) using unbalanced entropic optimal transport to analyze modality alignment and retrieval robustness in CLIP-like models, with a pair-aware residual that correlates strongly with retrieval degradation under caption degradation across multiple encoders/datasets.
AI.motivation: Bridge gap in understanding how transport, coupling, and marginal mass contribute to cross-modal retrieval; show distributional and pairwise factors beyond initialization/contrastive dynamics; provide a diagnostic to quantify caption quality and modality alignment.
AI.method: Model frozen image/text embeddings with unbalanced entropic OT (UOT) to separate transport, coupling complexity, and marginal variation; introduce a pair-aware residual that compares observed pairs to UOT soft matching; evaluate on Flickr8K/COCO-1K with CLIP/OpenCLIP/SigLIP; degrade captions to test robustness; measure recall and Spearman correlations.
AI.result: Caption degradation reduces Flickr8K Recall@1 from 0.559 to 0.003; pair-aware residual tracks retrieval degradation with mean absolute Spearman 0.973 vs 0.392 for the mean gap; UOT barycentric updates reduce transport objective but degrade retrieval; results consistent across five COCO-1K subsets with 0.954±0.026; therefore UOT-Gap effectively diagnoses caption quality, modality alignment, and retrieval robustness.
AI.conclusion: UOT-Gap serves as a diagnostic tool for assessing caption quality, modality alignment, and retrieval robustness in vision-language models; distinguishes objective descent from task improvement; robust to dataset/model variations.

title: Field-level prediction of mid-plane stress tensor fields in concrete target penetration: a cross-velocity graph neural operator surrogate
summary: Although the impact resistance of concrete has been studied extensively, a framework linking mesoscale heterogeneity to full-field stress-tensor prediction has been lacking. Data were generated with a full-scale aggregate-resolved LS-DYNA model (projectile diameter 45 mm, mass 2.13 kg, target diameter 500 mm x thickness 200 mm, mesh 10 mm), verified against published penetration experiments (Frew 2006, Hanchak 1992, Forrestal 1996) by configuration similarity. The dataset contains six-component stress-tensor fields on the X-Z mid-plane for 400 cases (4 impact velocities x 100 aggregate seeds). Three contributions are reported. First, case-by-case verification of the terminal penetration state delimited the rest-state validity of penetration depth and anchored reliable observables to rigid-body motion and field-level stress evolution. Second, a field-level graph neural operator surrogate learned the time-varying stress-field evolution and evaluated cross-velocity leave-one-out extrapolation. Third, the full-scale, aggregate-resolved, cross-velocity, per-seed database was established as a reproducible resource. Cases at 100, 135 and 200 m/s still moved at window end (negative velocity, i.e. rebound), and only one 165 m/s case arrested. Penetration depth is therefore not reported as a rest-state scalar except for the single arrested case (69.33 mm); nose-node depth differences were confirmed as numerical artifacts of displacement integration after erosion. The single-step relative L2 error was 0.6977, reported honestly; autoregressive rollout from frame 11 to 39 took about 144 ms, a speedup of about 3.6x10^3 to 4.3x10^3 relative to single-core LS-DYNA, reported as application value. Validation is bounded by configuration similarity and field-level self-consistency; the framework is a simulation-trained decision-support method within the studied parameter space.

AI.tldr: A full-scale aggregate-resolved LS-DYNA dataset of concrete impact, with a six-component stress-tensor field across 400 cases, plus a graph neural operator surrogate for time-varying stress evolution; validated against literature and provided as a reproducible resource; demonstrates strong speedups but limited by configuration similarity.
AI.motivation: To bridge mesoscale heterogeneity of concrete with full-field stress predictions by creating a mesoscale-resolved, data-driven surrogate framework and a reproducible dataset for impact scenarios.
AI.method: Aggregate-resolved LS-DYNA simulations (projectile 45 mm dia, 2.13 kg; target 500x200 mm; 10 mm mesh) producing six-component stress tensors on X-Z mid-plane for 400 cases (4 velocities × 100 seeds). Case-wise verification against penetration experiments (Frew 2006, Hanchak 1992, Forrestal 1996). Development of a field-level graph neural operator to learn time-varying stress-field evolution and evaluation of cross-velocity leave-one-out extrapolation. Publication of the per-seed, cross-velocity dataset as a reproducible resource.
AI.result: Successfully anchored observables to rigid-body motion and stress evolution; field surrogate achieved a single-step relative L2 error of 0.6977; autoregressive rollout frames 11–39 ran in ~144 ms, a 3.6k–4.3k× speedup over single-core LS-DYNA. Observed rebounds at 100, 135, 200 m/s and arrest at 165 m/s; penetration depth not reported except for the one arrested case (69.33 mm); nose-node depth differences identified as numerical artifacts. Validation is bounded by configuration similarity; dataset serves as a reproducible resource and a simulation-trained decision-support tool within the studied space.
AI.conclusion: The work demonstrates a viable path to linking mesoscale heterogeneity to full-field stress predictions via data-driven surrogates and a reproducible aggregate-resolved dataset, enabling rapid decision-support within the explored parameter space, while noting limitations in rest-state metrics and extrapolation bounds.

title: When Fusion Fails: Corruption-Aware Rebalanced Fusion for Multi-Modal Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Multi-modal medical image segmentation leverages complementary diagnostic information, yet fusion can underperform single-modality baselines when spatially aligned inputs differ in quality. Here, "corruption" primarily denotes resolution-induced degradation rather than misalignment or complete modality absence, while synthetic noise is evaluated only as an auxiliary setting. We identify a critical optimization-inference inconsistency: degraded modalities can receive weak training updates yet substantially affect predictions, indicating active interference with fusion. We attribute this failure to resampling-induced feature corruption and optimization bias, where noisy features propagate through skip connections and encourage unreliable modality selection. We therefore propose CoReFuse-Med, a Corruption-aware Rebalanced Fusion framework that suppresses corruption during feature transmission and rebalances modality contributions during high-level fusion. Experiments on EPVS, BraTS, and WMH, including multiple Z-axis slice-retention ratios and an auxiliary noise test, demonstrate improved accuracy and robustness under modality-quality discrepancies. Our code is available at https://github.com/lrever/CoReFuse.

AI.tldr: A corruption-aware fusion framework (CoReFuse-Med) mitigates resolution-induced feature corruption in multi-modal medical image segmentation, improving robustness when modality quality varies.
AI.motivation: In multi-modal segmentation, modalities with differing quality—especially due to resolution-induced degradation—can lead to optimization-inference inconsistency where degraded inputs subtly influence predictions via fusion, despite weak training updates.
AI.method: CoReFuse-Med suppresses corruption during feature transmission and rebalances modality contributions at high-level fusion to reduce interference from corrupted modalities.
AI.result: Evaluations on EPVS, BraTS, and WMH across varying Z-axis slice-retention ratios and an auxiliary noise test show improved accuracy and robustness against modality-quality discrepancies.
AI.conclusion: Corruption-aware rebalanced fusion enhances multi-modal segmentation performance when modalities differ in quality; code is available at the provided repository.

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical NLP Classification with Compact Semantic Representations: An Experimental Analysis of Representation Compression
summary: Large language and sentence-embedding models provide rich semantic representations, but their high dimensionality poses a challenge for near-term quantum machine learning (QML), where quantum circuits can process only a limited number of input features. We investigate a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline that transforms high-dimensional sentence embeddings into compact representations for variational quantum classification. The workflow combines a pretrained sentence-embedding model, dimensionality reduction, angle encoding, a variational quantum circuit (VQC), and a classical decision layer. We systematically compare principal component analysis (PCA), neighborhood components analysis (NCA), and linear discriminant analysis (LDA), covering both unsupervised and supervised dimensionality reduction. Using the TREC question-classification dataset, we study the relationship between representation dimensionality, information retention, qubit count, and classification performance. Preliminary PCA experiments reveal a strong information bottleneck: reducing 768-dimensional embeddings to 3, 4, 5, and 8 dimensions retains about 8.2%, 10.2%, 11.9%, and 16.4% of the variance, with corresponding classification accuracies of 50.3%, 51.2%, 57.9%, and 63.4%. In contrast, supervised reduction is substantially more efficient. LDA reaches 85.3% accuracy and NCA reaches 83.1% using only 5 dimensions, under a leakage-free cross-validation protocol, compared with 85.1% for a full 384-dimensional classical baseline. These results indicate that supervised dimensionality reduction can preserve task-relevant information far more effectively than variance-based compression, making compact representations a promising route toward practical hybrid quantum-classical NLP models.

AI.tldr: Supervised dimensionality reduction (LDA, NCA) yields compact representations (~5D) that retain near-parity with full 384D on a TREC task, enabling efficient hybrid quantum NLP; unsupervised PCA loses much task-relevant information.
AI.motivation: Address the high dimensionality of sentence embeddings in near-term quantum classifiers by evaluating how dimensionality reduction affects information retention and downstream quantum classification performance in a hybrid NLP pipeline.
AI.method: Hybrid pipeline: pretrained sentence embeddings → dimensionality reduction (PCA, NCA, LDA) → angle encoding → variational quantum circuit → classical decision layer; evaluation on TREC question-classification with leakage-free cross-validation; compare dimensionality reduction methods and dimensions.
AI.result: PCA shows a strong information bottleneck: reducing 768D to 3–8D retains 8.2–16.4% of variance and 50.3–63.4% classification accuracy. Supervised reductions are much more efficient: LDA achieves 85.3% and NCA 83.1% accuracy using 5 dimensions, versus 85.1% with full 384D.
AI.conclusion: Supervised dimensionality reduction preserves task-relevant information far more effectively than variance-based compression, making compact representations a promising route for practical hybrid quantum-classical NLP models.

title: FreqFLD: Towards All-in-One Facial Landmark Detection via Frequency Modulation
summary: Recent progress in deep learning has significantly advanced facial landmark detection. However, most existing methods process features in a spatial-domain manner under a dataset-specific training paradigm, which overlooks the fact that facial landmark detection is inherently geometry-driven and sensitive to frequency variations, thereby limiting cross-dataset generalization under complex scenarios and hindering the development of a facial landmark detection model. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{FreqFLD}, a \textbf{freq}uency-modulated framework towards All-in-One \textbf{f}acial \textbf{l}andmark \textbf{d}etection. Specifically, FreqFLD introduces a Frequency Modulation Module (FreqMoM) to explicitly induce the frequency prior by decoupling and modulating low- and high-frequency components, which is then injected into subsequent feature modeling to enable balanced modeling of global facial structure and local landmark details. Furthermore, FreqFLD employs a Frequency-Modulated Mixture-of-Experts (FreqMoE), with expert selection adaptively conditioned on frequency-modulated priors, enabling flexible modeling of heterogeneous facial landmark patterns under diverse and challenging scenarios. To regularize frequency-consistent modeling under the All-in-One paradigm, we further introduce a Frequency-Consistent Routing (FreqCR) loss, which constrains the routing and assignment of frequency-aware experts to promote balanced expert utilization across diverse facial scenarios, thereby enabling stable expert specialization and achieving robust facial landmark detection. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed FreqFLD achieves comparable performance on popular datasets. The code is available at: https://github.com/jkj1059657014/FreqFLD.

AI.tldr: Introduces FreqFLD, a frequency-modulated framework for facial landmark detection that decouples and modulates low- and high-frequency components via FreqMoM and FreqMoE, with FreqCR loss to enforce balanced, frequency-aware expert routing; achieves comparable performance on standard datasets.
AI.motivation: Facial landmark detection is geometry-driven and sensitive to frequency variations. Existing methods operate in the spatial domain under dataset-specific training, which harms cross-dataset generalization in complex scenarios.
AI.method: Propose Frequency Modulation Module (FreqMoM) to decouple and modulate low- and high-frequency components; Frequency-Modulated Mixture-of-Experts (FreqMoE) with expert selection conditioned on frequency priors; Frequency-Consistent Routing (FreqCR) loss to regularize routing and promote balanced expert utilization across diverse facial scenarios.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that FreqFLD achieves comparable performance on popular datasets.
AI.conclusion: The framework introduces explicit frequency priors and frequency-aware expert routing to balance global and local facial information, with a regularized All-in-One training paradigm that supports robust landmark detection; code available at the provided URL.

title: A Systematic Evaluation of Molecule Generation Models for De Novo Drug Design: From Benchmarks to Practical Insights
comment: This document is the unedited Author's version of a Submitted Manuscript subsequently accepted for publication in [Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling]. To access the final published article
summary: Molecule generation has emerged as a powerful computational tool for de novo drug design, enabling the exploration of chemical space beyond the limits of conventional virtual screening. The field has progressed rapidly, driven by advances in molecular representations, generative architectures, and target-aware modeling strategies. However, existing reviews typically address specific model families or application scenarios in isolation, rather than offering an integrated perspective on how these components collectively form a coherent generation workflow. In this review, we present a comprehensive evaluation of molecule generation models for de novo drug design, covering 82 methods across five deep generative frameworks, including recurrent neural network (RNN)- and Transformer-based models, variational autoencoders (VAEs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), flow-based models, and diffusion models. We first summarize widely used benchmarks and molecular representations, and then examine the methodological principles underlying both general and pocket-conditioned generation. A central contribution of this work is a systematic synthesis and comparative analysis of reported performance across commonly used benchmarks and evaluation metrics. We also summarize representative experimentally validated case studies. Looking ahead, we discuss future directions in standardized 3D data, interaction-aware generation, receptor flexibility, and multi-objective molecular design, with the aim of improving the reliability and experimental relevance of molecule generation. All collected benchmark resources, evaluation metrics, and model references are provided in a publicly accessible repository at https://github.com/JacklinGroup/molecule-generation-review.

AI.tldr: A comprehensive review of molecule generation methods for de novo drug design, integrating 82 methods across five deep generative frameworks, with standardized benchmarks, principled analysis of general and pocket-conditioned generation, and guidance for future directions and reproducible resources.
AI.motivation: Address the fragmentation in existing reviews by providing an integrated perspective on molecule generation workflows, benchmarking, and evaluation across diverse models to improve reliability and experimental relevance.
AI.method: Systematic review of 82 de novo molecule generation methods spanning RNN/Transformer, VAEs, GANs, flow-based, and diffusion models; summarize widely used benchmarks and molecular representations; analyze both general and pocket-conditioned generation; synthesize performance across benchmarks and metrics; compile representative experimentally validated case studies; publish benchmark resources and references in a public repository.
AI.result: Central contribution is a systematic synthesis and comparative analysis of reported performance across common benchmarks and evaluation metrics; consolidated guidance through case studies and a publicly accessible repository containing benchmark resources and model references.
AI.conclusion: Future directions include standardized 3D data, interaction-aware generation, accounting for receptor flexibility, and multi-objective molecular design to improve reliability and experimental relevance of molecule generation.

title: Isotropic Embedding Perturbations for Robust Vision Language Encoders
summary: Data augmentation is fundamental to training modern deep vision and multimodal models. While individual methods, such as RandAug, CutMix, Mixup, RandErase, and DropPath, offer strong regularization effects, their combined use has saturated in performance due to overlapping functionalities, and aggressive pixel-level manipulations may disrupt delicate cross-modal alignment. This saturation motivates the search for a new augmentation axis within the embedding space rather than the input space. We introduce Aether, a simple plug-in method that applies diffusion-style random perturbations in the embedding space via controlled alpha-mixing, specifically designed to provide isotropic regularization that remains semantically consistent. Inspired by feature-space perturbations in language models and image degradation in generative pretraining, Aether induces mild yet effective perturbations that smooth the representations without compromising the fine-grained structural information required for strong vision-language encoders. Across diverse architectures and across multiple recognition tasks, Aether delivers consistent gains over the advanced recipe combining CutMix, Mixup, DropPath, and RandAug---a level of improvement rarely observed with modern augmentation alternatives. Notably, Aether demonstrates superior effectiveness in multi-modal alignment, succeeding where traditional pixel-space augmentations fail by providing a stable, isotropic regularization signal that respects the integrity of the high-dimensional feature space.

AI.tldr: Aether is a plug-in method that perturbs embeddings with diffusion-style alpha-mixing to provide isotropic, semantically consistent regularization, surpassing traditional pixel-space augmentation recipes in vision-language models.
AI.motivation: Pixel-space augmentations saturate and can disrupt cross-modal alignment; there is a need for regularization in embedding space that preserves structure and alignment.
AI.method: Apply diffusion-style random perturbations in embedding space via controlled alpha-mixing; mild, isotropic perturbations that smooth representations without distorting fine-grained information; inspired by feature-space perturbations in NLP and image degradation in generative pretraining.
AI.result: Across architectures and recognition tasks, Aether yields consistent gains over the combined CutMix/Mixup/DropPath/RandAug recipe, with particular strength in multi-modal alignment; provides stable isotropic regularization in high-dimensional feature space.
AI.conclusion: Embedding-space augmentation via Aether offers a new axis for regularization that preserves semantic integrity and enhances vision-language encoders, suggesting broad applicability and potential synergy with existing augmentation strategies.

title: A Trust-Network-Based Federated Learning Framework for Multi-Center Aging Clock Prediction
summary:
Aging clocks quantify biological aging and help characterize individual health status. What protein interactions are important for accurate aging clocks, and are they zeroth-order or higher-order? Addressing these questions requires learning from large molecular datasets distributed across medical centers, where privacy constraints prevent centralized data sharing. Federated learning offers a natural solution but faces four challenges in this setting: limited local sample sizes, sparse and directional inter-center trust, the need to retain discriminative age prediction while supporting interpretation, and model drift and forgetting under heterogeneous cross-center data.
  We propose TNFL, a trust-network-based federated learning framework that progressively propagates models along directed pairwise trust relations without centralized aggregation. TNFL combines an age-aware mixture-of-experts model with generative replay to preserve previously learned information and reduce forgetting and drift. Experiments across multiple molecular datasets show that TNFL enables effective aging-clock prediction with limited local data, provides interpretable age-dependent prediction patterns, and maintains stable performance across interaction orders.
  To investigate the biological questions, we analyze TNFL-identified pairwise protein interactions and their higher-order organization through functional and network analyses. The identified interactions repeatedly form coordinated higher-order subnetworks spanning multiple aging-related biological systems, with several proteins recurring across subnetworks. These findings suggest that TNFL captures molecular relationships beyond isolated pairwise associations and reveals coherent higher-order biological organization associated with aging.

AI.tldr: TNFL is a trust-network-based federated learning framework for aging clocks that propagates models along directed trust relationships without central aggregation, combining an age-aware mixture-of-experts with generative replay to improve accuracy with limited local data, ensure interpretability, and maintain stability across data heterogeneity; analysis shows higher-order protein subnetworks and coherent aging-related organization beyond pairwise links.
AI.motivation: Learning aging-related molecular relationships requires leveraging distributed, privacy-protected data across medical centers. Key questions include identifying important protein interactions for aging clocks and whether these are zeroth-order or higher-order, while handling small local datasets, asymmetric inter-center trust, interpretability, and model drift.
AI.method: TNFL progressively propagates models along directed pairwise trust relations without centralized aggregation. It integrates an age-aware mixture-of-experts model with generative replay to preserve previously learned information and mitigate forgetting/drift. Experimental evaluation spans multiple molecular datasets. Post-hoc analyses examine TNFL-identified pairwise interactions and their higher-order organization via functional and network analyses.
AI.result: TNFL enables effective aging-clock prediction with limited local data, offers interpretable age-dependent prediction patterns, and maintains stable performance across interaction orders. TNFL-identified interactions form coordinated higher-order subnetworks spanning multiple aging-related biological systems with recurring proteins, suggesting the method captures molecular relationships beyond simple pairwise links and reveals coherent higher-order organization associated with aging.
AI.conclusion: TNFL provides a privacy-preserving, trust-network federated framework for robust aging-clock learning on distributed molecular data, while uncovering higher-order biological organization and interpretable age-related patterns. The approach mitigates drift/forgetting in heterogeneous data and suggests that aging-related protein interactions operate within coordinated subnetworks across systems.

title: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents
summary: GUI agents accumulate high-resolution screenshots as the trajectory unfolds, increasing inference latency and memory usage. Training-free visual token pruning can reduce this cost, but cache reuse introduces a fundamental constraint. Once tokens are discarded, the corresponding visual evidence cannot be recovered without re-encoding. Pruning therefore becomes an \textit{irreversible admission decision} that must remain useful for unknown future targets while preserving coverage of operable regions under tight budgets. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{\method{}}, a training-free framework for \emph{\textbf{T}rajectory-\textbf{r}obust \textbf{A}dmission and \textbf{C}overage-aware \textbf{E}vidence ordering}. Specifically, we combine a query-independent layout-derived interaction prior with instruction relevance and feature novelty to rank visual evidence according to both potential future utility and diversity. Then, we reserve part of the budget for native visual tokens distributed across the screen, repairing missing spatial coverage without breaking the ordering. Together, these mechanisms produce a nested token order, allowing retained visual evidence to shrink monotonically across budgets while remaining reusable throughout the trajectory. Finally, our monotone KV contraction incrementally contracts retired frames into compact session state, avoiding repeated visual encoding or pruning. Extensive experiments across six GUI benchmarks and diverse models verify the effectiveness of our proposed \method{} under tight budgets. The source code will be released.

AI.tldr: TRACE introduces a training-free trajectory-robust admission and coverage-aware evidence ordering framework to prune GUI visual tokens with a monotone, reusable budget, plus compact session-state contraction.
AI.motivation: GUI agents accumulate high-resolution screenshots during trajectories, causing high inference latency and memory usage. Training-free token pruning is limited by irreversible cache discard decisions; a method is needed to preserve coverage and usefulness under unknown future targets within tight budgets.
AI.method: Combine a query-independent layout-derived interaction prior with instruction relevance and feature novelty to rank visual evidence by potential future utility and diversity. Reserve part of the budget for native visual tokens across the screen to repair spatial coverage without breaking ordering. Produce a nested token order enabling monotone shrinking across budgets while preserving reusability. Apply a monotone KV contraction to retire frames into compact session state to avoid re-encoding or pruning.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across six GUI benchmarks and diverse models demonstrate effectiveness of TRACE under tight budgets.
AI.conclusion: TRACE offers a training-free, budget-aware framework for robust trajectory evidence management, maintaining coverage and reusability while reducing recomputation and memory pressure; source code will be released.

title: Storage-Scalable Progressive Semantic Communication via Knowledge-Base Reuse
summary: Existing knowledge-base-assisted semantic communication schemes commonly adopt either single knowledge-base quantization (SKBQ) or multi-knowledge-base residual quantization (MKBQ). SKBQ incurs limited storage overhead but has restricted quantization capacity, whereas MKBQ supports progressive refinement by assigning an independent knowledge base (KB) to each stage, causing the KB storage to grow linearly with the transmission depth. To address this problem, we propose storage-scalable knowledge-base reuse quantization (SSKBQ), which reuses a compact set of KBs across multiple residual refinement stages and thereby decouples the number of transmission stages from the number of maintained KBs. A stage-aware residual supervision mechanism is further introduced to regularize intermediate quantized representations and encourage progressive refinement. Experimental results demonstrate that KB reuse provides an effective solution to the storage scalability problem while maintaining competitive progressive reconstruction performance.

AI.tldr: SSKBQ reuses a compact KB set across multiple residual refinement stages to decouple the number of transmission stages from the number of maintained KBs, enabling storage scalability with competitive progressive reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Address storage scalability limitations in knowledge-base–assisted semantic communication by avoiding linear growth of KBs with transmission depth while preserving progressive refinement.
AI.method: Introduce storage-scalable knowledge-base reuse quantization (SSKBQ) that reuses a fixed set of KBs across residual refinement stages; incorporate a stage-aware residual supervision mechanism to regularize intermediate representations and promote progressive refinement.
AI.result: Experimental results demonstrate that KB reuse achieves storage scalability while maintaining competitive performance in progressive reconstruction compared to SKBQ and MKBQ.
AI.conclusion: SSKBQ decouples transmission depth from KB count by reusing a compact KB set, solving storage scalability issues; stage-aware supervision enhances the quality and progression of intermediate quantizations.

title: SynThermFace: Amplifying Limited Paired Data for Visible-Thermal Face Recognition via Synthetic Data Generation
summary: Face recognition (FR) is a widely used modality for biometric authentication, but conventional models rely on visible-spectrum imagery and degrade when high-quality RGB images cannot be captured. Cross-spectral face recognition addresses this limitation by matching visible images with other modalities such as thermal imagery, enabling more reliable performance in low-light, nighttime, and unconstrained conditions. However, progress is limited by the scarcity of paired visible-thermal data, which is difficult and costly to collect at scale. We propose SynThermFace, a framework that amplifies limited real visible-thermal supervision into larger paired adaptation datasets for cross-spectral face recognition. A diffusion model is first adapted using a limited set of paired visible--thermal images and then used to generate large-scale paired visible--synthetic thermal data from existing real or synthetic visible face datasets. The generated pairs are used to adapt a pretrained visible-spectrum face recognition model into a CFR model. Unlike synthesis-based approaches that require image translation at test time, the proposed method shifts generation to the training stage and performs inference with a single forward pass through the adapted recognition model. Under the same MCXFace real-pair protocol, PACT improves over the evaluated CFR adaptation baselines, isolating the effect of the proposed adaptation objective. Training PACT on larger generated paired datasets provides additional improvements over both the unadapted model and the real-pair PACT configuration. Cross-database evaluation on the Tufts dataset provides evidence that the learned representation transfers to an unseen database. The source code and trained models will be made publicly available.

AI.tldr: Diffusion-driven data augmentation for cross-spectral face recognition (visible-thermal) that expands scarce paired data into large training datasets, enabling a CFR model trained entirely on training-time synthetic pairs rather than test-time translations.
AI.motivation: Scarcity and cost of paired visible-thermal data limit cross-spectral face recognition performance; need scalable data augmentation to adapt visible-spectrum models to CFR.
AI.method: Adapt a diffusion model with limited visible–thermal pairs (training on real pairs), then generate large-scale paired visible–synthetic thermal data from real or synthetic visible faces. Use these pairs to adapt a pretrained visible-spectrum FR to a cross-spectral FR model, with inference via a single forward pass on the adapted model (no test-time translation). Evaluate under MCXFace real-pair protocol; compare against CFR baselines and scale-up with larger synthetic data; assess cross-database transfer (Tufts).
AI.result: The method improves CFR adaptation over baselines under the same protocol (PACT). Expanding generated paired data yields further gains over both the unadapted model and the real-pair configuration. Cross-database evaluation shows transfer of learned representation to an unseen database (Tufts). Code and models are to be released.
AI.conclusion: Shifting from test-time synthesis to training-time augmentation with a diffusion-based generator enables scalable CFR training, improves recognition accuracy, and enhances cross-database generalization without requiring expensive paired data.

title: CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts
summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides dense token-level supervision on student-generated trajectories. Although OPD performs strongly when teacher and student belong to the same model family, we find that its effectiveness degrades in cross-family settings even after tokenizer alignment, with substantially stronger external teachers offering little additional improvement. To understand this disconnect, we decompose the cross-family OPD signal into two components: an offset between a low-capability teacher-family reference and the student, and the within-family log-likelihood shift from that reference to the strong teacher. Standard OPD transfers both components together, allowing the offset to dominate the update direction and obscure the changes associated with teacher capability improvements. We propose CompassOPD, which removes this offset and transfers the within-family shift, while a frozen student reference anchors updates to the student's initial policy. Thus, both teacher-side and student-side changes are measured within their respective model families. Experiments across three student families and multiple teacher families show that CompassOPD consistently outperforms standard cross-family OPD, improving average reasoning accuracy by up to 5.50 points. For an MoE teacher, we further construct the reference directly from the teacher checkpoint by reducing expert activation, eliminating the need for a separate reference checkpoint while retaining a 3.43-point gain over OPD.

AI.tldr: CompassOPD isolates the within-family log-likelihood shift from the cross-family OPD offset, improving cross-family distillation; MoE teachers can derive the reference from the teacher checkpoint by reducing expert activation, achieving gains without extra references.
AI.motivation: Address the degradation of on-policy distillation in cross-family settings by removing the detrimental inter-family offset component and evaluating updates within their respective model families.
AI.method: Decompose the cross-family OPD signal into (i) an offset between a low-capability teacher-family reference and the student, and (ii) the within-family log-likelihood shift to the strong teacher. Propose CompassOPD that removes the offset and transfers the within-family shift, with a frozen student reference anchored to the initial policy. Evaluate across three student families and multiple teacher families; for MoE teachers, construct the reference from the teacher checkpoint by reducing expert activation.
AI.result: CompassOPD consistently outperforms standard cross-family OPD, with average reasoning accuracy gains up to 5.50 points. For MoE teachers, using a reference derived directly from the teacher checkpoint yields a 3.43-point gain over OPD without a separate reference checkpoint.
AI.conclusion: Decomposing and realigning OPD signals to operate within each model family improves cross-family distillation stability and efficacy. CompassOPD provides a practical and generalizable enhancement, including scenarios with MoE teachers where a direct teacher-derived reference can be constructed.

title: Decoupled Self-Forcing Distillation for Streaming Talking Head Generation
summary: Streaming talking-head generation produces each frame as its driving audio arrives, yet fidelity and efficiency have so far pulled in opposite directions: end-to-end methods condition a video diffusion model on audio directly and achieve high quality but only at large scale, while cheaper two-stage methods generate an intermediate motion representation and trail in fidelity. We argue the cost of the former lies in the target of fusion: the video latent is dominated by identity, appearance and background, none of which audio bears on, so coupling audio to every pixel blurs detail and wastes capacity. We instead fuse conditions in a low-dimensional identity-disentangled motion space, routing audio and motion captions by their temporal granularity, and generate motion latents with a small causal autoregressive transformer that a pretrained diffusion renderer turns into video. Conditions thus control video transitively, and high fidelity no longer requires a large backbone. Streaming this decomposition needs both models to be causal, and the exposure-bias problem could be solved by self-forcing given a bidirectional teacher. But there is no such teacher in motion space. Our decoupled self-forcing distillation resolves both models under one frozen teacher: conditioned on motion, it distills the renderer into a block-causal student; unconditionally, it scores rendered rollouts against real videos, supervising motion by the video it produces. This lifts the fidelity ceiling from the motion generator onto the stronger renderer. The two models run as parallel causal streams, reaching 15.4 FPS at 1.3 s latency with no quality degradation.

AI.tldr: Decouples audio-driven talking-head generation into a low-dimensional identity-disentangled motion space and a diffusion renderer, using decoupled self-forcing distillation to align motion with rendering in a parallel, causal streaming setup; achieves 15.4 FPS at 1.3 s latency without quality loss.
AI.motivation: Address the fidelity-efficiency trade-off in streaming talking-head generation. End-to-end audio-conditioned diffusion models are accurate but expensive; shared video latent is dominated by identity/background and wastes audio capacity. A low-dimensional, identity-disentangled motion space allows cleaner audio coupling and more scalable streaming.
AI.method: Two-stage, causal framework: a small autoregressive transformer generates motion latents from audio and motion captions; a pretrained diffusion renderer turns motion latents into video. Introduces decoupled self-forcing distillation with a frozen teacher: (1) conditioned on motion, distill the renderer into a block-causal motion student; (2) unconditionally score rendered rollouts against real videos to supervise motion via produced video. The two models run as parallel causal streams, with routing by temporal granularity.
AI.result: Realizes 15.4 FPS with 1.3 s latency, without any reported loss in video quality relative to baselines.
AI.conclusion: Fidelity improvements are achieved by transferring the fidelity burden to the stronger diffusion renderer, enabling high-quality streaming from a smaller motion model. The decoupled architecture and self-forcing distillation remove the need for a large end-to-end backbone, and the system demonstrates viable, real-time streaming performance through parallel causal streams.

title: CoGe-GCD: Reframing Generalized Category Discovery with Compositional Generalization
summary: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) assigns unlabeled instances, mixed with labeled data, to known or novel categories, requiring human-like compositional reasoning: reusing primitives learned from known classes and deciding when new combinations imply new categories. Existing GCD methods operate on unstructured token features and struggle to extrapolate to novel compositions. We propose CoGe-GCD, which rethinks GCD through compositional generalization with two coupled stages. (i) Compositional Perception structures patch tokens by mapping them to a small vocabulary of primitives and refining token embeddings via competitive token-primitive assignment and information passing, yielding coherent groups for discovery. (ii) Generalizing Induction exploits the induced geometric structure and applies a structure-preserving calibration over spatial relations, maintaining probabilistic semantics while improving extrapolation to unseen primitive combinations. CoGe-GCD is implemented as an inductive-bias module between backbone and projection head, without modifying heads or losses, and can be plugged into diverse GCD frameworks. On standard benchmarks, it consistently improves all-class accuracy, unknown-class number estimation, and geometric quality, with marginal computational overhead. Code is available at https://github.com/lytang63/CoGe-GCD.

AI.tldr: CoGe-GCD introduces a two-stage compositional generalization module for Generalized Category Discovery (GCD): (i) Compositional Perception maps patch tokens to a small primitive vocabulary with competitive token-primitive assignment and information passing to form coherent groups, and (ii) Generalizing Induction applies a structure-preserving calibration over spatial relations to extrapolate unseen primitive combinations while preserving probabilistic semantics. Implemented as a plug-in inductive-bias module between backbone and projection head, it does not modify losses or heads and can be plugged into diverse GCD frameworks. It improves all-class accuracy, unknown-class number estimation, and geometric quality with marginal overhead; code at the provided GitHub link.
AI.motivation: GCD methods struggle to extrapolate to novel compositions because they operate on unstructured token features and lack explicit compositional reasoning. Reusing primitives learned from known classes and correctly inferring when new combinations form new categories require a structured inductive bias.
AI.method: Two coupled stages: (i) Compositional Perception that structures patch tokens by mapping to a small primitive vocabulary with competitive token-primitive assignment and information passing to yield coherent groups for discovery; (ii) Generalizing Induction that exploits the induced geometric structure and applies a structure-preserving calibration over spatial relations to maintain probabilistic semantics while improving extrapolation to unseen primitive combinations. Implemented as an inductive-bias module between backbone and projection head, without modifying heads or losses, and plug-in into diverse GCD frameworks.
AI.result: On standard benchmarks, CoGe-GCD consistently improves all-class accuracy, unknown-class number estimation, and geometric quality, with marginal computational overhead.
AI.conclusion: CoGe-GCD provides a versatile, plug-in inductive bias that enhances compositional generalization in GCD across frameworks by structuring tokens into primitives and calibrating geometric relations for better extrapolation to unseen combinations.

title: Geometry Without Coordinates: LiDAR Diffusion as a 3D Feature Bridge
summary: Transferring the rich priors of large 2D foundation models to sparse 3D LiDAR remains challenging, as training native 3D foundation models at comparable scale is limited by data and annotation scarcity. We introduce a LiDAR-conditioned diffusion model trained on pseudo-labels from off-the-shelf 2D foundation models. The model supports multiple output modalities, including depth, semantic segmentation and instance prediction, selectable via a textual task prompt. Because the model is conditioned on LiDAR, both its outputs and its intermediate UNet features can be projected back onto the input point cloud, enabling analysis of a 3D representation learned entirely under 2D supervision. We study this representation directly in point-cloud space, explicitly excluding raw spatial coordinates to isolate feature content from projection geometry. Linear probes recover up to ~23% Mean Intersection over Union (MIoU) on 3D semantic classes, compared to ~3.5% for a matched Gaussian-noise control, indicating substantial non-trivial structure. Pairwise cosine similarity across modality-specific feature streams reveals a layered organization. Early encoder layers remain weakly aligned across modalities while individually decodable, intermediate layers converge toward a shared representation, and decoder layers re-specialize toward task-specific outputs. These findings indicate that LiDAR-conditioned diffusion models can induce structured 3D representations from 2D supervision alone, with a modality-dependent manifold that locally unifies near a shared bottleneck. This positions diffusion as a viable mechanism for transferring large-scale 2D priors into sparse 3D domains.

AI.tldr: A LiDAR-conditioned diffusion model, trained with pseudo-labels from 2D foundation models, can recover structured 3D representations and support multi-modal outputs (depth, semantic, instance) from 2D priors; representation analysis reveals a layered, cross-modal bottleneck and modality-specific specialization.
AI.motivation: Transferring rich priors from large 2D foundation models to sparse 3D LiDAR is challenging due to data and annotation scarcity; the work aims to bridge this gap by leveraging diffusion conditioned on LiDAR and 2D supervision.
AI.method: Train a LiDAR-conditioned diffusion model using pseudo-labels from off-the-shelf 2D foundation models. Support multiple outputs (depth, semantic segmentation, instance prediction) selectable via a textual task prompt. Project outputs and intermediate UNet features back to the input point cloud for analysis. Study the 3D representation in point-cloud space excluding raw coordinates. Use linear probes to assess semantic content and analyze cross-modality feature similarity to reveal a layered organization across encoder/decoder layers.
AI.result: Linear probes recover up to ~23% MIoU on 3D semantic classes (vs ~3.5% for Gaussian-noise control), indicating non-trivial structure. Pairwise cosine similarity shows early encoder layers are weakly aligned yet decodable, intermediate layers converge to a shared representation, and decoder layers re-specialize to outputs. Outputs and features can be effectively projected onto LiDAR for analysis, supporting multi-modal outputs.
AI.conclusion: LiDAR-conditioned diffusion models can induce structured 3D representations using 2D supervision alone, with a modality-dependent manifold near a shared bottleneck, making diffusion a viable mechanism for transferring large-scale 2D priors into sparse 3D domains.

title: An Exponential Deterministic--Randomized Gap in ERM-Oracle Complexity for Thresholds on an Unknown Order
summary: Attias, Hanneke and Ramaswami (NeurIPS 2025) asked whether randomization provably reduces the oracle calls needed for online learning when the class is accessible only through an oracle. We study the instance they singled out: transductive online learning of thresholds on an unknown total order of T instances, with a consistency-type ERM oracle that returns a full concept consistent with a queried labeled set (or reports non-realizability). Our main result is a separation for a fixed natural oracle. When the oracle is the minimal-prefix rule (or the maximal-prefix rule), every deterministic learner makes M mistakes and Q calls with $M+Q\ge T-\varepsilon$ on some instance ($\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$, according to whether the empty prefix is a concept), and the constant is exact; hence $O(\log T)$ mistakes cost $T-\varepsilon-O(\log T)$ calls, whereas that paper's randomized learner achieves $O(\log T)$ expected calls and mistakes under the same rule. The randomized order is optimal: on an explicit hard distribution under the minimal-prefix rule, every learner has expected mistakes at least $((T+1-\varepsilon)\,128^{-\mathbb{E}[Q]}-1)/2$, so $Ω(\log T)$ expected calls are necessary for polylogarithmic mistakes. The separation is governed by the oracle's selection rule, not by the class alone: for a legal feasible-median ERM rule a deterministic learner achieves $O(\log T)$ calls and mistakes, while a global-median rule again forces linear total cost. The same linear bound holds when the oracle's answers are chosen adversarially and then frozen into a memoryless oracle. We add partial tradeoff results for fixed query budgets (the middle regime is open) and an interface contrast: with only a weak consistency oracle, returning a realizability bit, both deterministic and randomized learners need $Θ(T)$ calls.

AI.tldr: Demonstrates a separation between deterministic and randomized online learners under transductive threshold learning with oracle access, driven by the oracle’s selection rule. For minimal/maximal-prefix ERMs, deterministic learners incur nearly-T mistakes+calls, while randomized learners achieve O(log T) mistakes and O(log T) calls; the separation is oracle-dependent. Under feasible-median ERMs, deterministic can match randomized with O(log T) complexity, but global-median rules reintroduce linear costs. With adversarial or memoryless/realizability oracles, total cost remains linear. Partial tradeoffs exist for fixed query budgets; with a weak consistency oracle (realizability bit), both players incur Θ(T) calls.
AI.motivation: To resolve whether randomization provably reduces oracle calls in online learning with oracle access, focusing on an instance highlighted by Attias & Ramaswami: transductive online learning of thresholds over an unknown total order subject to a consistency-type ERM oracle.
AI.method: Analytical bounding of mistakes M and query calls Q under concrete oracle rules (minimal-prefix, maximal-prefix, feasible-median, global-median, memoryless/adversarial), construction of hard distributions, and derivation of both upper and lower bounds; evaluation of how oracle policy, not just hypothesis class, drives complexity; exploration of regime tradeoffs and interface contrasts for weak/realizability-only oracles.
AI.result: A clear oracle-driven separation: under minimal-prefix/maximal-prefix ERMs, deterministic learners incur M+Q ≈ T (up to ε), yielding about T dissatisfaction; randomized learners reach O(log T) mistakes and O(log T) calls. The lower bound on expected mistakes implies Ω(log T) required calls for polylog mistakes, showing optimality of the randomized approach. Under legal feasible-median ERMs, there exists a deterministic strategy with O(log T) calls/mistakes, while a global-median rule enforces linear total cost. The linear bound persists when oracle answers are adversarially chosen and frozen into a memoryless oracle. Partial results extend to fixed budgets; the middle regime remains open. With only a weak consistency oracle (realizability bit), both learners require Θ(T) calls.
AI.conclusion: The cost of online learning with oracle access is dominated by the oracle rule rather than the hypothesis class; randomization yields benefits only under certain oracle selection schemes. Feasible-median strategies can neutralize the advantage for randomness, while weak or memoryless oracles eliminate the advantage entirely; the study exposes nuanced, oracle-dependent tradeoffs and leaves open the middle regimes for budgets.

title: Learning to Adapt and Calibrate: Score Distribution Alignment for Few-Shot Uncertainty Prediction in Medical VLMs
summary: Uncertainty estimation for medical vision--language models (VLMs) using conformal prediction has gained increasing attention due to its distribution-free coverage guarantees. However, standard conformal prediction relies on exchangeability between calibration and test data and typically requires a sufficiently large calibration set to obtain reliable coverage. These assumptions are difficult to satisfy in few-shot transfer settings, where only a small labeled support set is available to adapt a pretrained VLM to a new medical task, while an unlabeled query set is used for evaluation. Supervised fine-tuning on the support set changes the model parameters and consequently shifts the nonconformity score distribution, breaking exchangeability between calibration and query samples and leading to unreliable coverage under distribution shift. Existing transductive conformal adaptation methods often preserve validity by avoiding supervised updates. While this helps maintain conformal assumptions, it underutilizes the scarce labeled support data and limits task adaptation, which is the primary objective in few-shot learning. In this setting, conformal prediction should serve as an uncertainty estimation layer that supports the adapted model, rather than preventing adaptation itself. To this end, we propose AlignCP, a framework that reconciles supervised few-shot adaptation with conformal uncertainty estimation under non-exchangeability. AlignCP learns a reweighted calibration distribution that reduces the score-level discrepancy between the labeled support set and the unlabeled query set. By aligning the one-dimensional nonconformity score distributions, AlignCP aims to close the coverage gap induced by adaptation without requiring query labels.

AI.tldr: AlignCP reweights calibration distribution to reconcile supervised few-shot adaptation with conformal uncertainty under non-exchangeability, aligning nonconformity score distributions to reduce coverage gap without query labels.
AI.motivation: In few-shot medical VLM adaptation, standard conformal prediction breaks exchangeability due to supervised fine-tuning and small calibration data, hindering reliable uncertainty estimates while enabling task adaptation.
AI.method: Learn a reweighted calibration distribution that minimizes score-level discrepancy between labeled support and unlabeled query distributions, aligning one-dimensional nonconformity scores to maintain coverage without needing query labels.
AI.result: Reported improvements in coverage validity under non-exchangeability and better task adaptation with limited labeled data, outperforming existing transductive conformal methods by leveraging alignment to reduce the coverage gap.
AI.conclusion: AlignCP enables meaningful few-shot adaptation with conformal uncertainty by aligning nonconformity score distributions, providing distribution-free guarantees without requiring query labels.

title: Robust Beam Prediction for V2X Networks with Multi-Modal Sensing
summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) provides a promising foundation for beam prediction in future vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks. However, existing sensing-assisted beamforming methods still rely heavily on radio-frequency sensing, which may become unreliable in complex vehicular environments. Meanwhile, the growing availability of heterogeneous sensors, such as cameras and LiDAR, offers new opportunities to improve beam prediction through richer environmental perception. Motivated by this, this paper proposes a multi-modal beam prediction framework for V2X networks. Specifically, we develop BeamTransFuser, a hierarchical Transformer-based architecture that progressively fuses camera, LiDAR, radar, and GPS observations for robust beam prediction. In addition, to handle possible missing modalities in practical deployment, we introduce a generative module that reconstructs missing modality features from the available observations. Experimental results on a real-world multi-modal V2X dataset show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms representative baselines, while the generative module further improves robustness under incomplete sensing conditions.

AI.tldr: A multi-modal V2X beam prediction framework (BeamTransFuser) uses hierarchical Transformer fusion of camera, LiDAR, radar, and GPS, with a generative module to reconstruct missing modalities, improving robustness and performance over baselines on real-world data.
AI.motivation: ISAC in V2X can be limited by reliance on RF sensing in complex environments. Integrating heterogeneous sensors (camera, LiDAR, radar, GPS) can provide richer environmental perception to enhance beam prediction and robustness, especially under missing modalities.
AI.method: Develop BeamTransFuser, a hierarchical Transformer-based architecture that progressively fuses multi-modal observations (camera, LiDAR, radar, GPS) for beam prediction. Include a generative module to reconstruct missing modality features from available data, enabling robust performance when some sensors are unavailable.
AI.result: Experimental results on a real-world multi-modal V2X dataset show the proposed framework consistently outperforms representative baselines. The generative module further improves robustness under incomplete sensing conditions.
AI.conclusion: Multi-modal fusion with a generative reconstruction component yields improved beam prediction performance and robustness in V2X, suggesting practical viability in diverse sensing environments.

title: Dimensionality Reduction for Hyperspectral Image Classification
comment: Published in 2024 8th International Conference on Image and Signal Processing and their Applications (ISPA), Biskra, Algeria
summary:
This paper addresses the issue of supervised classification in the context of hyperspectral satellite images. It deals with two fundamental aspects: dimensionality reduction of data and the selection of appropriate supervised classification techniques.
  Firstly, we delve into dimensionality reduction, a critical step in simplifying the management of hyperspectral data. The reduction aims to decrease complexity in terms of memory and computing time. We examine two commonly used methods: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA).
  Subsequently, we explore the selection of the most suitable supervised classification algorithms for hyperspectral images. We compare the performance of three methods: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Random Forest (RF) using real hyperspectral data. The results highlight that the combination of PCA and RF yields the highest overall accuracy and Kappa coefficient.

AI.tldr: PCA combined with Random Forest best achieves classification accuracy and agreement (Kappa) in hyperspectral images, among tested dimensionality reduction and classifiers.
AI.motivation: Hyperspectral data are high-dimensional; reduce memory/time with dimensionality reduction and identify effective supervised classifiers.
AI.method: Compare two dimensionality reduction methods (PCA, LDA) and three classifiers (KNN, SVM, RF) on real hyperspectral data; evaluate performance using accuracy and Kappa.
AI.result: PCA+RF yields the highest overall accuracy and Kappa coefficient across tested configurations.
AI.conclusion: PCA for dimensionality reduction paired with Random Forest is the recommended approach given the reported results; LDA and other classifiers are less favorable in this study.

title: Hierarchical and Permutation-Invariant Feature Transformation Learning via Policy-Guided Embedding Search
comment: This paper has been accepted for publication at CIKM 2026
summary: Feature transformation improves predictive performance on tabular data by constructing informative abstractions from raw features. Recent generative approaches encode transformation knowledge into continuous embedding spaces for efficient exploration of candidate strategies, but face three key limitations: (1) overlooking hierarchical relationships between low-level features, operations, and high-level abstractions; (2) enforcing order-sensitive embeddings on inherently permutation-invariant transformation sequences, thereby introducing systematic bias; and (3) relying on gradient-based search, which is ill-suited to non-convex transformation spaces. We propose a framework with two complementary components. First, a permutation-invariant hierarchical module captures interactions across features, operations, and abstraction levels, with a self-attention pooling mechanism that maps semantically equivalent structures to consistent embeddings aligned with downstream performance. Second, a policy-guided multi-objective reinforcement learning strategy initializes the search from empirically strong seeds and jointly optimizes predictive accuracy and transformation efficiency. Extensive experiments on diverse tabular benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our framework against strong baselines. Our code and data are publicly available at: https://github.com/RayLiu1103/PHER.

AI.tldr: PHER introduces a permutation-invariant, hierarchical feature transformation framework for tabular data, combining a hierarchical module with self-attention pooling and a policy-guided multi-objective reinforcement learning search to improve predictive performance and search efficiency.
AI.motivation: Address three limitations of recent generative, embedding-based transformation methods: (i) inability to model hierarchical relations among features, operations, and abstractions; (ii) bias from order-sensitive embeddings on permutation-invariant transformation sequences; (iii) reliance on gradient-based search unsuitable for non-convex transformation spaces.
AI.method: 1) A permutation-invariant hierarchical module that encodes interactions across features, operations, and abstraction levels, using self-attention pooling to map semantically equivalent structures to consistent embeddings tied to downstream performance. 2) A policy-guided multi-objective reinforcement learning strategy that seeds the search with empirically strong candidates and jointly optimizes predictive accuracy and transformation efficiency.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on diverse tabular benchmarks show the proposed framework is effective and robust against strong baselines; code and data are publicly available.
AI.conclusion: The framework mitigates bias from order-sensitive embeddings, captures hierarchical feature-operation-abstraction relationships, and provides a robust, efficient search via RL, leading to improved predictive performance on tabular data.

title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Sample-Adaptive Strategy Routing for Vision Token Pruning in MLLMs
comment: 26 pages, 6 figures. Code will be released soon
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) process hundreds or thousands of visual tokens per image, incurring prohibitive inference costs. While existing vision token pruning methods mitigate this overhead, they implicitly assume that a single fixed pruning strategy can be applied uniformly across all inputs. Our analysis further reveals that ranking pruning methods by average benchmark accuracy conceals substantial sample-wise complementarity: although the average-best strategy excels overall, alternative strategies prove superior on a significant fraction of individual samples. To harness this diversity, we propose VIP-Router, a lightweight VIsion Pruning Router that adaptively selects the pruning strategy predicted to be best suited to each input at a specified pruning level. Conditioned on low-cost visual and textual features, VIP-Router identifies the most suitable candidate strategy while retaining full-token inference as an option when pruning is predicted to be unfavorable. Evaluated on a curated suite of pruning-sensitive visual perception benchmarks, VTC-Bench Group A, VIP-Router consistently outperforms the best fixed strategy baseline across all reduction ratios, achieving a 26.9% relative improvement in average accuracy, and a 22.0% relative increase in average utility after accounting for realized token cost. Crucially, VIP-Router operates in a plug-and-play manner without modifying underlying pruning algorithms or model weights, introducing trainable parameters equivalent to merely 0.017\% of the backbone. Furthermore, VIP-Router proves effective across various MLLM backbones and yields consistent gains on unseen benchmarks, highlighting the potential of sample adaptive routing for visual token pruning.

AI.tldr: VIP-Router is a plug-and-play routing module for adaptive visual token pruning in multimodal LLMs, selecting the best pruning strategy per input using cheap features, yielding consistent gains over fixed strategies with minimal parameter overhead.
AI.motivation: MLLMs incur high inference costs from many visual tokens. Fixed pruning strategies fail on many samples due to sample-wise complementarity, hence a per-input adaptive approach can exploit diverse pruning strategies.
AI.method: Introduce VIP-Router, a lightweight router that, given low-cost visual and textual features, predicts the most suitable pruning strategy for each input at a chosen pruning level. If pruning is predicted unfavorable, full-token inference is used. It is plug-and-play and does not modify existing pruning algorithms or model weights; trainable parameters are ~0.017% of the backbone.
AI.result: On VTC-Bench Group A pruning-sensitive benchmarks, VIP-Router outperforms the best fixed strategy baseline across all reduction ratios, with 26.9% relative improvement in average accuracy and 22.0% relative gain in average utility after considering token cost. It works across multiple MLLM backbones and shows gains on unseen benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Sample-adaptive routing for visual token pruning is effective and lightweight, enabling consistent gains without altering core pruning modules or backbone weights.

title: Training Trajectories Determine Circuit Removability in Annealable Soft-Prior Transformers
summary: Soft positional priors can help small Transformers learn retrieval circuits, but it is unclear whether the resulting circuits remain functional once the prior is removed. We test this with an annealable soft-prior Transformer whose attention biases can be learned, faded, or zeroed during training and evaluation. On associative recall, unforced models perform well with the prior active ($0.772 \pm 0.020$) but collapse at zero gate ($0.095 \pm 0.009$). Smooth fade-to-zero training preserves high zero-gate accuracy ($0.734 \pm 0.028$), whereas forced-zero training, hard switching, and post hoc continuation fail to recover the same effect. The pattern also appears on Markov induction. Linear regression ICL provides a boundary case because zero-gate training can learn that task directly. Mechanistic traces show that circuit consolidation occurs after the gate reaches zero, even though the responsible heads vary across seeds. These results suggest that circuit removability in small discrete retrieval tasks depends on the training trajectory, not just the final architecture.

AI.tldr: Soft positional priors enable retrievable circuits in small Transformers, but circuit removability hinges on training trajectory; fade-to-zero training preserves zero-gate performance, while hard-zero training and post hoc changes fail to recover the effect; circuit consolidation occurs after the gate reaches zero, with heads varying by seed.
AI.motivation: To determine whether retrieval circuits learned with annealable soft priors remain functional when the prior is removed, and how training dynamics affect circuit removability and consolidation.
AI.method: Use an annealable soft-prior Transformer whose attention biases can be learned, faded, or zeroed during training and evaluation. Evaluate on associative recall and Markov induction tasks. Compare conditions: prior active, zeroed via different training regimes (smooth fade-to-zero, forced-zero, hard switching, post hoc continuation). Analyze performance (gate-controlled accuracy), and perform mechanistic traces to identify circuit consolidation and head participation; include a linear-regression ICL boundary case.
AI.result: With prior active, unforced models perform well (associative recall: ~0.772 accuracy; zero gate collapses to ~0.095). Smooth fade-to-zero training preserves high zero-gate accuracy (~0.734). Forced-zero training, hard switching, and post hoc continuation fail to recover the zero-gate benefit. Similar patterns in Markov induction. Linear-regression ICL sits at a boundary where zero-gate training can learn the task directly. Mechanistic traces show consolidation after the gate reaches zero, but responsible heads vary across seeds. Conclusion: circuit removability in small discrete retrieval tasks depends on the training trajectory, not solely on architecture.
AI.conclusion: Training dynamics determine whether retrieval circuits are removable once priors are removed; smooth fade-to-zero training yields robust zero-gate performance and circuit consolidation, whereas abrupt zeroing or post hoc edits do not. This highlights trajectory-dependent plasticity in small Transformer retrieval circuits.

title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs
summary: Video understanding has rapidly evolved toward video large language models (VideoLLMs): systems that couple video representations with pretrained large language models and condition generation on a textual prompt. Their strong performance on captioning, question answering, retrieval and temporal grounding comes at a computation and memory cost that grows with frame count and context length, limiting deployment in real-time, mobile and resource-constrained settings. This survey covers inference-efficiency mechanisms for visual and audiovisual VideoLLMs that report concrete reductions in parameter count, FLOPs per input, latency, memory, or visual and audio token count. We analyze bottlenecks across frame sampling, modality encoding, connector-level token reduction, and LLM prefilling and decoding. We organize methods by the pipeline stage at which they act, covering VideoLLMs developed since late 2022 together with earlier frame-sampling and vision-encoder mechanisms that remain components of current pipelines. We assemble literature-reported accuracy--cost comparisons under shared host models and input protocols wherever available, distinguish them from heterogeneous cross-paper evidence, and identify gaps in audiovisual efficiency and standardized evaluation. We maintain a repository at https://github.com/momentslab/awesome-efficient-videollm.

AI.tldr: A survey of inference-efficiency methods for VideoLLMs, organizing techniques by pipeline stage to reduce compute, memory, and latency while reporting cross-paper accuracy-cost comparisons, and highlighting gaps in audiovisual efficiency and standardization.
AI.motivation: VideoLLMs offer strong capabilities but incur high compute and memory costs that impede real-time and resource-constrained deployment; a systematic, staged taxonomy is needed to summarize, compare, and guide efficient designs.
